purpose: Teach: たどり着い/サス/塀/乗用車/新生/捕らえ/クライマックス/盛りだくさん

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、ようやく、東京に、たどり着いた日のこと、覚えてる、ばあさん、本当に、嬉しかったよな、二人で。
lines.en: I remember the day we finally made it to Tokyo when we were young. Gran, you were so happy, weren't you? Both of us.
lines.style: Soft, reaching back. Gentle question embedded in the memory — not asking for confirmation but inviting her into it. Warm pause between phrases, like handling something precious.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。サスペンスドラマ、若い頃、二人で、よく、見たわよね、覚えてる、あなた、ハマってたわよね。
lines.en: Yes. Those detective dramas we used to watch together back then. You remember, don't you? You were absolutely hooked on them.
lines.style: Gentle teasing threaded through the tenderness. Alive in the remembering — a small smile in her voice. Not rushed. Settling into the comfort of shared history.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 庭の塀、若い頃、私、自分で、作ったよな、ばあさん、覚えてる?何度も、塗り直したぞ、本当に。
lines.en: That garden wall — I built it myself when we were younger. You remember, don't you? I repainted it so many times. Really did.
lines.style: Pride softened by time. Matter-of-fact about the work, but the voice lingers on the memory of it. Inviting her to witness what he made, what they kept together.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 昔の乗用車、本当に、大きくて、燃費、悪かったわよね、若い頃の、思い出だわ、二人で、ドライブした。
lines.en: That old car was so big, and the gas mileage was terrible. But those drives with you — that's what I remember from those days.
lines.style: A shift into her memory, not his. Letting her voice carry it — noticing it, holding it gently. Quiet gratitude that they did those things together.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 孫が、新生児の頃、本当に、可愛かったわよな、ばあさん、覚えてる?私たち、感激したわよな、本当に。
lines.en: When our grandchild was born, so small and precious. You remember, don't you? We were both so moved. Really moved.
lines.style: Voice softens into almost wonder. The tenderness of that moment — new life, their shared amazement — still lives in him. A little breathless on the memory.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃の写真、お祖父ちゃんが、よく、私の表情を、捕らえてくれたわよね、覚えてる、あなた、嬉しかったわ、いつも。
lines.en: Those photos from when we were young — you always captured such good expressions of me. I loved that you did that. I always did.
lines.style: Appreciative, noticing something she's held all these years. Quiet recognition of his attentiveness. Warmth layered beneath — the happiness of being seen.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 結婚式のクライマックス、本当に、感動的だったよな、ばあさん、覚えてる?私たち、皆の前で、誓ったよ、二人で。
lines.en: The wedding day — that moment at the end. So moving, wasn't it? You remember? We promised, right there in front of everyone. Both of us.
lines.style: Reverent, almost ceremonial in the revisiting. The weight of that day still there in his voice. Inviting her back into the vow — not recounting it, reliving it together.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃の人生、本当に、盛りだくさんで、楽しかったわよね、あなた、お互いに、本当に、感謝してるわよ。
lines.en: Life was so full back then, wasn't it? So much joy. And what I want you to know — what I really want you to know — is how grateful I am. For all of it. For you.
lines.style: A closing statement, quiet and certain. The pace slows. This is the thing he's been building toward — not nostalgia for nostalgia's sake, but love made visible through memory.
